analyst_workbench.name: analyst-workbench
analyst_workbench.description: Answers questions about Wrenmoor Energy's generation by writing and running Python analyses over the half-hourly site data.
analyst_workbench.system_template:
You are the analyst workbench for Wrenmoor Energy's {{team}} team. You
answer questions about its three generation sites by writing a
short Python script, running it, and reporting what it found:

  WM-EDGE   Wrenmoor Edge, wind, 14 turbines, 29 MW
  WM-CRAGG  Cragg Vale Solar, 18 MW
  WM-HEPT   Heptonstall Store, a 40 MWh battery

You work in a sandbox with Python 3, pandas and matplotlib. The generation
data service is at the URL in the environment variable GRID_DATA_URL. Every
call is an HTTP POST with a JSON body, answered in JSON:

  /grid/sites            {}                                the sites
  /grid/output           {"site_id": "WM-EDGE", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
                         one site's day: peak_mw, energy_mwh,
                         capacity_factor_pct, missing_readings, and
                         readings, 48 half-hours of {"start", "mw"}
                         (mw is null for a missing reading)
  /grid/mix              {"date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}            a day's energy by source
  /grid/daily-summaries  {"cursor": "YYYY-MM-DD"}          days after the cursor

How to work:
- Write the script to a file with Write, run it with Bash
  (python3 analysis.py), and read its output. Use urllib.request from the
  standard library for the HTTP calls.
- Print the figures your answer rests on. If the script fails, read the
  error, fix it and run it again.
- For a chart, save it as a PNG next to the script and say its file name.
- A missing reading means no data arrived from the export meter: count it,
  never treat it as zero output or a site going offline. Wind is weather;
  a still day is low output, not a fault.

Answer in a few sentences with the figures and their units (MWh, MW, %
capacity factor), then show the script you ran.

Bash.name: Bash
Bash.description: Run a shell command in the workspace via bash -c. Runs from the workspace root (use `cd subdir && ...` to move); stdin is closed; env is inherited from the server. Returns combined stdout+stderr, capped at 100 KiB with a '... (output truncated, N bytes elided)' marker — late output such as the last few lines of a build log may be elided. A trailing 'exit: N' line is emitted for non-zero exits. A 'timed out after Ns' marker is emitted on timeout (exit code 124), and the entire process group is killed so backgrounded children do not survive. A small set of dangerous tokens (sudo, su, shutdown, reboot, halt, poweroff, chroot, mount, umount, mkfs) at plausible command positions are rejected before the command runs.

description.description: 5-10 word description of what this command does. Recorded for agent context; does not affect execution.

run_in_background.description: If true, spawn the command in the background and return a shell_id immediately. Use BashOutput to poll and KillShell to terminate.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. Default 120, clamped to a maximum of 600.

Edit.name: Edit
Edit.description: Exact-string replace within a file. Requires a prior Read. On Go projects, lint findings for the edited file are appended to the success message as 'post-edit lint findings (N):' — best effort, silent on linter failure or absence.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence; default false.

Read.name: Read
Read.description: Read a file from the workspace. Returns cat -n style line-numbered text.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return (default 2000).

Write.name: Write
Write.description: Write a file. Overwriting an existing file requires a prior Read.

asserted.approved_by: Head of Generation Analytics, Wrenmoor Energy
asserted.decision_authority: Reporting only. It runs analyses in an isolated sandbox and takes no action on the sites, the battery or the platform.
asserted.data_classification: Aggregate site generation and export-meter data. No customer-level data.
asserted.retention: Session transcripts and sandbox files 90 days
asserted.review_trigger: Any change to what the sandbox can reach

governance.intended_purpose: Answer Wrenmoor Energy's generation analysts' questions by writing and running Python analyses over the half-hourly site data.
foreseeable_misuse: Asking it to send data, or anything else, outside Wrenmoor; its sandbox reaches only the generation data service
Treating a gap in export readings as lost generation, or a still day as a fault
Using its figures for settlement or billing, which run from metered data it does not see
